questions.question: `library(readr)` has already run in this session. A student writes `readr::read_csv("wage.csv")` where `read_csv("wage.csv")` would also do. How do the two calls differ?
options: The prefixed call first reinstalls readr from CRAN, so it always uses the newest version.
Only the prefixed call works; `library()` does not make the short name available.
Both read the file in the same way; the prefix only shows which package it comes from.
Only the short call works; the prefix is meant for packages that are not loaded.

questions.question: A script you share with classmates uses `read_csv()`. Why should the line `install.packages("readr")` be removed or commented out, while `library(readr)` stays at the top?
options: Installing is needed once per computer; left in, it downloads readr on every run.
`library(readr)` installs readr by itself when it is missing, so the line is redundant.
Once readr is installed, it is loaded at every start-up, as stats is, so neither line is needed.
`install.packages()` also loads the package, so keeping both lines would load readr twice.

questions.question: In a session where readr is installed but `library(readr)` has not been run, what does `readr::read_csv("wage.csv")` do?
options: It fails with `could not find function`, because readr has not been loaded with `library()`.
It reads `wage.csv` from a folder called `readr` inside the working directory.
It loads the whole readr package for the session and then calls `read_csv()`.
It calls `read_csv()` from the installed readr package without loading the package.

questions.question: Yesterday a student ran `install.packages("readr")`. Today, in a new R session, `read_csv("wage.csv")` stops with `could not find function "read_csv"`. Which line should the student run first?
options: `install.packages("readr")`
`library(readr)`
`library(read_csv)`
`exists("read_csv")`

questions.question: On a computer with a fresh R installation, `library(readr)` stops with an error saying that there is no package called readr. What is the fix?
options: Write `library("readr")` with quotation marks, as when installing it.
Call `readr::read_csv()` instead, which works without the package.
Restart R, so that every available package is loaded at start-up.
Run `install.packages("readr")` once, then `library(readr)` again.

questions.question: readr is installed. In a fresh session, a script runs `d <- read_csv("wage.csv")` on its first line and `library(readr)` on its second line. What happens?
options: The first line stops with `could not find function "read_csv"`.
R reads the whole script first, loads readr, and then reads the file.
The first line works, because readr is installed on this computer.
The first line reads the file with `read.csv()` instead and continues.

questions.question: A script starts with the two lines `# install.packages("readr")` and `library(readr)`. A classmate who has never installed readr runs the whole script. What happens?
options: R runs the first line, installs readr from CRAN and then loads it with the second.
R notices that readr is missing and runs the commented install line by itself.
The `#` line is skipped, and `library(readr)` stops because readr is not installed.
`library(readr)` gives no message, and the script stops at the first `read_csv()` call.

questions.question: Which call returns a single `TRUE` or `FALSE` saying whether `quantile` is one of the objects of the stats package?
options: `quantile %in% ls("package:stats")`
`"quantile" %in% ls("package:stats")`
`"quantile" %in% ls(stats)`
`ls("package:stats") %in% "quantile"`

questions.question: readr was installed and used on Monday. In which situation must `install.packages("readr")` be run again before `library(readr)` works?
options: After restarting R on the same computer, with an empty workspace.
When a new script file that uses `read_csv()` is created and opened.
On a new computer, or after installing a new version of R.
After changing the working directory to another folder with `setwd()`.

questions.question: In a fresh session, `"cor" %in% ls("package:base")` returns `FALSE`, yet `cor(x, y)` works without any `library()` call. Why?
options: R fetches `cor()` from CRAN the first time it is called and installs it.
`cor()` belongs to stats, which comes with R and is loaded at start-up.
`ls("package:base")` lists only functions written in R, not built-in ones.
`cor()` is part of R itself and not of any package, so `ls()` skips it.

questions.question: readr is not yet installed. Which pair of lines, run in this order, installs it and then makes `read_csv()` available?
options: `install.packages(readr); library(readr)`
`library(readr); install.packages("readr")`
`library("readr"); library(readr)`
`install.packages("readr"); library(readr)`

questions.question: readr is installed. A script contains the line `library(Readr)` with a capital R. What happens when this line runs?
options: R stops with an error saying that there is no package called Readr.
R loads readr, because package names are not case-sensitive.
R loads readr and warns that the name should be written in lower case.
R stops with `could not find function "Readr"` and loads nothing.

questions.question: On a computer where readr has never been installed, what does `readr::read_csv("wage.csv")` do?
options: It stops with `could not find function "read_csv"`, as without `library()`.
It stops with an error saying that there is no package called readr.
It installs readr from CRAN first and then reads the file.
It falls back on `read.csv()`, which comes with R, and reads the file.
